lucretius.oneLineEn: Roman Epicurean poet who, in De Rerum Natura, uses atomism to cure fear of the gods and of death.

seneca.oneLineEn: Roman Stoic statesman developing practical ethics in letters and essays on anger, clemency, and finite life.

epictetus.oneLineEn: Roman Stoic teacher whose control dichotomy, assent training, and inner freedom define a practical handbook tradition.

marcus-aurelius.oneLineEn: Roman emperor and Stoic author who, in the Meditations, joins cosmic order, duty, and self-discipline.

fichte.oneLineEn: Advanced Kant's critical philosophy into a freedom system grounded in self-activity (Wissenschaftslehre).

schelling.oneLineEn: Organized nature, spirit, art, and freedom into German Idealism's most generative systematic experiments.

feuerbach.oneLineEn: Inverted Hegelian theology into humanist critique of religion; a near gateway for Marx's early alienation critique.

pascal.oneLineEn: Reshaped early modern Christian apologetics through human fragility, reason's limits, and the wager.

peirce.oneLineEn: Founded scientific American pragmatism through inquiry logic, the pragmatic maxim, and triadic semiotics.

james.oneLineEn: Linked psychology, religious experience, free will, and pragmatic truth into radical empiricist pluralism.

du-bois.oneLineEn: Advanced racial experience as modern political philosophy via double consciousness, color line, and abolition democracy.

moore.oneLineEn: Helped form Cambridge analytic philosophy via ethical non-naturalism, anti-idealism, and common-sense realism.

popper.oneLineEn: Remade 20th-c. philosophy of science and politics through falsifiability, critical rationalism, and the open society.

kuhn.oneLineEn: Rewrote historical philosophy of scientific progress via paradigms, normal science, and scientific revolutions.

dilthey.oneLineEn: Brought the historical life-world into method via Geisteswissenschaften, Erlebnis, and Verstehen.

gadamer.oneLineEn: Extended hermeneutics from method to ontology via effective history, fusion of horizons, and linguisticality.

jaspers.oneLineEn: Connected Kierkegaard, Nietzsche, Heidegger, and Arendt through Existenz, limit situations, and the Axial Age.

sextus-empiricus.oneLineEn: Preserved ancient Pyrrhonism in the Outlines and Against the Professors, a hub for early modern skeptical revival.

duns-scotus.oneLineEn: Scholastic link between Aquinas and Ockham via univocity of being, formal distinction, and individuation theory.

al-kindi.oneLineEn: Founding figure of Arabic philosophy uniting the Greek translation movement, first philosophy, and Islamic monotheism.
